package_info.why_malicious: This package version contains a known vulnerability (CVE-2018-5968) that allows incomplete blacklist protection, leading to potential deserialization of untrusted data. Attackers can exploit this to execute arbitrary code or perform other malicious actions.

execution_context.file_location: application code using jackson-databind for deserialization

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
Object obj = mapper.readValue(untrustedInput, Object.class);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes untrusted input using jackson-databind, which due to incomplete blacklist, may allow instantiation of dangerous classes, leading to arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data without proper validation or blacklisting is a common vector for remote code execution attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects deserialization libraries to prevent instantiation of dangerous classes; this version fails to do so.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization of trusted, validated data is legitimate in many applications.

attack_chain.action: Application receives untrusted input and attempts to deserialize it using jackson-databind.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential instantiation of dangerous classes and arbitrary code execution.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data using vulnerable jackson-databind versions
Lack of class blacklist enforcement during deserialization
file_indicators: Code patterns invoking ObjectMapper.readValue on untrusted sources
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections following deserialization (if exploited)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan dependency manifests for vulnerable jackson-databind versions (<=2.0.4). Review code for deserialization of untrusted input. Monitor for exploit attempts targeting deserialization endpoints and for abnormal process/network activity following deserialization operations.
